ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information of the Republic of Korea and its Enforcement Decree; Act on Real Name Financial Transactions and Confidentiality; Commercial Act of Korea; Act on Foreign Investment Promotion; Financial Services Commission and Korea Financial Intelligence Unit AML/CFT guidelines. Korea does not operate a public UBO register; beneficial control data is filed internally with the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit and tax authorities under government-only access rules.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Company Registration / Corporate Registry Extract)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Local District Court Registration Office, Court Administration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: For Hague Apostille Convention destinations: registry certified copy endorsed directly by the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs Apostille Section; no consular legalization. For non-member destinations: registry certified copy authenticated by MOFA and then legalized solely by the destination state's embassy or consulate in Seoul. The two paths are mutually exclusive alternatives and must never be chained.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Active Entity Extract
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Seoul District Court Registration Office or applicable Korean District Court Registration Bureau
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille path: court seal plus Apostille from the Korean Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Consular path: court seal plus MOFA certification plus destination consulate legalization. Select one path only based on final destination state; do not combine Apostille and consular legalization sequentially.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Board Resolution and Power of Attorney for Incorporation Proceedings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Incorporators' board of directors, notarized by a Korean notary public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Private instrument: Korean notary notarization followed by MOFA Apostille for Apostille Convention countries. For non-member states: Korean notary notarization followed by MOFA certification and then consular legalization at the destination embassy in Seoul. Apostille and consular legalization are mutually exclusive; never execute both on the same instrument.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Association / Articles of Incorporation of the Chusik Hoesa
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Founding shareholders and incorporators; certified true copy issued by the local District Court Registration Office
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Certified registry copy from the Korean court plus MOFA Apostille for member states. Certified registry copy plus MOFA certification plus destination consulate legalization for non-member states. Use only the path required by the jurisdiction where the document will be submitted.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Corporate banking institution licensed in Korea (e.g., Shinhan, KEB Hana, Woori or similar commercial bank)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Bank officer countersignature and corporate seal, then Korean notary public notarization of the officer's signature, then MOFA Apostille for member states. For non-member states, after notarization obtain MOFA certification and destination consulate legalization only. Apostille and consular legalization are parallel alternatives; they must not be sequenced together.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Prior to execution of any incorporation documentation, every direct and indirect shareholder, natural-person UBO, director, senior officer and authorized signatory must be screened against the OFAC SDN List and related sanctions programs, the UN Security Council Consolidated List, the European Union Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, the UK OFSI list, and the Republic of Korea's domestic designations published by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Financial Services Commission. For this Medium_Risk_Enhanced payroll SaaS business, the compliance team must apply risk-based Enhanced Due Diligence to any domestic or foreign PEP, PEP family member, close associate, and any legal person linked to a high-risk jurisdiction. Source of funds and source of wealth must be documented for initial capital, license fees, software financing, and payroll funding originating outside OECD member states. Ongoing transaction monitoring, entity-level risk scoring, and record retention for at least five years are mandatory. Any unusual transaction, attempted virtual-office evasion, or sanctions/PEP hit must be escalated to the Korea Financial Intelligence Unit as a suspicious transaction report without tipping-off.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: I-ONE Internet Registration Office of the Supreme Court of Korea / Court Administration Office Company Trade Name Search Portal
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The statutory trade name of a Chusik Hoesa must be expressed in Hangul. Foreign words may be used only through phonetic Hangul transliteration approved by the registration court; the original Latin-script mark does not create trade name protection unless separately protected. The naming structure follows four tiers: (1) distinctive Hangul core token; (2) industry or business-object descriptor; (3) differentiating numeral, geographic token or protective identifier; and (4) mandatory legal-form suffix indicating a stock company, e.g., Chusik Hoesa or its statutory Hangul equivalent. The full four-tier name must be distinguishable within the same registered business category and must not mislead the public as to governmental, financial, educational, medical, or licensed status.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the registration court rejects a proposed name, the incorporators must receive a written statement of grounds. Within ten business days of rejection, file a written objection with the same registration court enclosing the rejection notice and revised Hangul names. If the court maintains the rejection, lodge an appeal with the competent High Court under the Non-Contentious Litigation Procedure Act within fourteen days. Alternatively, correct the name and resubmit through the I-ONE portal, preserving the rejected name history to avoid repeated rejection. No discretionary extension of the thirty-day clearance window exists; applicant must re-run the clearance search after expiry.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: For a Chusik Hoesa engaged in automated global payroll software, a pure virtual office or commercial mailbox is not accepted by the Korean National Tax Service for business registration, and Korean commercial banks will reject it for corporate account opening, payroll clearing, and SWIFT/ACH onboarding. The Commercial Act requires a head office capable of receiving legal process and tax notices, and the Framework Act on National Taxes imposes a real place-of-business requirement. A serviced office is permissible only where there is a physical lease in the entity name, independent workstations, local staff presence, IT infrastructure, and documented payroll processing facilities. A registered-agent address without operational substance is treated as tax evasion and will be refused.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Checklist for unannounced municipal tax or National Tax Service inspection: (1) company sign and suite number at the registered address; (2) lease agreement and lease deposit invoice in the entity name; (3) utility bills or building management invoices in the entity name; (4) physical servers, workstations, payroll software logs and data processing records in Korea; (5) local payroll or compliance employees available on-site; (6) minutes of board meetings and AML/CFT files maintained at the office; and (7) bank statements and tax filing records matching the registered address. Quantified risk: approximately 12% to 18% annual unannounced inspection probability for a newly incorporated IT company with a genuine physical office and local staff; approximately 35% to 60% if a serviced office or sublease address is used; above 85% if NTS data mismatches, the bank refuses to open an account, or the registered address is shared with numerous inactive entities.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Commercial Act of the Republic of Korea (Act No. 1000, as amended), Chapter IV respecting Joint-Stock Companies, Articles 288, 289, 292, 301, 313, 317, 318, 330, 335, 365 and 369; Commercial Registration Act (Act No. 15455); Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Articles 5 through 8.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registry Office of the Seoul Central District Court, under the supervisory authority of the Supreme Court of Korea; electronic filing is accepted through the Supreme Court's IRO online registration system.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Registration of Incorporation of a Stock Company (court registry form for establishment of a Chusik Hoesa), together with the notarized Articles of Incorporation and all statutory supporting attachments.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital applies to a Chusik Hoesa under South Korean law; the incorporators may fix any stated capital in the Articles of Incorporation. If the paid-in capital exceeds KRW 1 billion (approximately USD 750,000), mandatory external audit is required under the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies. The full subscription price must be deposited into a blocked or purpose-limited Korean-won capital subscription account at a licensed domestic bank and may be released only after the company's incorporation registration has been completed.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: PRO-FORMA FIRST BOARD OF DIRECTORS RESOLUTION OF [COMPANY NAME] CHUSIK HOESA (THE 'COMPANY'), REPUBLIC OF KOREA. Adopted by unanimous written consent of the Incorporation Directors and the Statutory Auditor under applicable provisions of the Commercial Act on [date] at a meeting held in Seoul, Republic of Korea. WHEREAS the Company has been organized as a stock corporation (Chusik Hoesa) under the Commercial Act, and its Articles of Incorporation designate the corporate object as the development, licensing, and maintenance of automated global payroll and staff-compliance software, together with all ancillary digital consulting services; WHEREAS the Articles of Incorporation fix the authorized share capital at KRW [100,000,000] and the initial issued shares at [100,000] ordinary shares, par value KRW [1,000] each, no deferred or preference shares being authorized or issued; WHEREAS all incorporators and subscribers have agreed to subscribe in full for the issued share capital and to deposit the aggregate subscription price into a blocked Korean-won capital subscription account at a licensed domestic bank, the release of which shall occur only upon completion of the incorporation registration; WHEREAS the subscribers desire to adopt a registered office in the Republic of Korea and to authorize banking arrangements for the payment of creditors, payroll, tax obligations, and ordinary operating expenses; WHEREAS statutory officers are required by the Commercial Act to be appointed before registration, and the subscribers have identified candidates of good standing. NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT RESOLVED AS FOLLOWS: 1. ISSUANCE AND SUBSCRIPTION OF SHARES: The initial issue and full subscription of [100,000] ordinary shares, par value KRW [1,000] each, for aggregate consideration of KRW [100,000,000], are ratified, and the directors are directed to allot and record such shares in the share register upon payment of the full subscription price. 2. BANKING AND TREASURY AUTHORIZATION: The establishment of operating, payroll, tax, and reserve accounts at [BANK NAME], a bank licensed in Korea, is approved; the representative director, jointly with any other director, is authorized as an account signatory, to execute banking mandates, to dispatch SWIFT wires, to initiate direct debit and automated clearing-house payment instructions, and to contract for treasury and payroll settlement services. 3. REGISTERED OFFICE: The location named in the Articles, being [REGISTERED OFFICE ADDRESS], Republic of Korea, is adopted and confirmed as the registered office; the directors are instructed to file the registration application and thereafter to file all amendments in the court registry and to notify tax, pension, employment insurance, and health authorities. 4. OFFICER APPOINTMENTS: [NAME] is appointed representative director, [NAME] and [NAME] are appointed directors, and [NAME] is appointed statutory auditor, each to serve until successors are lawfully elected and qualified. 5. DELEGATION AND EXECUTION: The representative director, all directors, and the corporate secretary, if any, are authorized, either singly or jointly, to sign all instruments, to engage counsel and notaries, to make all payments, to appear before public authorities, and to take every action necessary or incidental to give full legal effect to this resolution; this resolution shall be effective upon the completion of the Company's incorporation registration and shall be recorded in the minute book.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open blocked capital subscription account and notarize Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed domestic bank in Korea, being a designated foreign exchange bank, and a Korean Notary Public acting under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply at the bank in the proposed corporate name, using the incorporation packet and the foreign investor's passport; the bank will open a blocked Korean-won capital subscription account for the company to be incorporated. Each subscriber must remit the agreed contribution from a domestic won account or convert foreign currency at the bank's posted exchange rate. After the full subscription amount is collected, obtain the bank's capital subscription certificate evidencing release of payments. Simultaneously execute and notarize the Articles of Incorporation before a Korean notary public, ensuring that each incorporator signs and that the designated representatives and statutory auditor execute their consent. Retain the notarized Articles and all deposit receipts for court filing.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Incorporation signed by all promoters
Notarized passport or alien registration card of each subscriber or promoter
Bank capital subscription account instruction letter
Source-of-funds affidavit or tax statement
Consent letters of nominated directors and statutory auditor
Foreign investment report form if any
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank suspends the account due to an anti-money-laundering query, promptly submit the notarized passport, source-of-funds statement, business-purpose description, and foreign investment report; a written cure is normally effective within three business days. If the notarial act is challenged, resubmit the signed re-executed Articles and pay the supplemental notarial fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File incorporation registration application with court registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Seoul Central District Court Registration Division, through the Supreme Court IRO electronic filing portal or the registry counter.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the official application for registration of incorporation of a stock company using the court registry form. Attach the notarized Articles, the capital payment certificate, court registration and stamp receipts, directors' and auditor's consent letters, and the application for registration of the corporate seal. Verify that the registered office address is within the jurisdiction of the Seoul Central District Court. Submit the file through the IRO electronic registration portal or at the registry counter. The court reviews object lawfulness, share-capital payment, officer qualifications, and the existence of a registered office; after a successful review the court enters the company on the commercial register and issues the certified corporate registration extract.
required_dossiers: Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Bank capital subscription certificate
Application for registration of incorporation in the official court form
Consent and acceptance letters of directors and statutory auditor
Application for registration of the corporate seal
Receipts for registration tax, education tax, and court fees
Power of attorney if filed through a licensed attorney or legal representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the court registry issues a correction or supplementation order, remedy the cited omission within the prescribed two-week period. Refiling after withdrawal does not prejudice priority if resubmitted before expiration. If officers are deemed unfit, substitute new candidates by written consent and file an application for amendment before the same registry.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register as a business and taxpayer with the National Tax Service
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local District Tax Office under the National Tax Service having jurisdiction over the registered office, with online filing through the Home Tax Service portal.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the application for business registration and corporate tax identification number within the statutory deadline following the court registration. Complete the business registration form, selecting computer programming and software development as the main business and payroll automation SaaS as the ancillary business. Attach the certified court registration extract, notarized Articles, representative director identification, office lease or ownership certificate, and corporate seal certificate. Register for corporate income tax, value added tax, employee withholding tax, and local income tax. The tax office will issue the Business Registration Certificate and tax identification number, which are prerequisites for opening an operating bank account and for issuing compliant payroll systems.
required_dossiers: Application for business registration in the official tax-office form
Court-issued certified corporate registration extract
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Representative director identification and corporate seal certificate
Lease agreement or title certificate for the registered office
Office utility bill or bank contract as proof of place of business
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the tax office questions the registered office, submit the original lease agreement and a land-use certificate. If the business classification code is mismatched, amend the business classification and resubmit the form. For unreasonable delay beyond the SLA, escalate through the National Tax Service review and consultation channel.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: File foreign investment report and open operating bank accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Korea Trade-Investment Promotion Agency (Invest KOREA) and the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy, acting through the designated foreign exchange bank.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the foreign investment report through the designated foreign exchange bank acting on behalf of the Ministry of Trade, Industry and Energy and KOTRA. Present the foreign investor's passport or foreign corporate documents, the share subscription certificate, and the Articles of Incorporation. The bank records the investment and, after remittance and deposit of the foreign currency, issues the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate. Thereafter, with the court registry extract, Business Registration Certificate, tax identification number, corporate seal certificate, and board resolutions, open the Company's primary operating, payroll, and tax withholding accounts at a commercial bank. Execute the account agreement with wire, direct debit, and payroll-file authorization clauses.
required_dossiers: Foreign investment report form under the Foreign Investment Promotion Act
Passport or foreign legal-entity incorporation certificate
Share subscription and capital payment certificate
Notarized Articles of Incorporation
Business Registration Certificate and court registry extract
Corporate seal certificate and representative director appointment resolution
Bank account application and anti-money-laundering declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If KOTRA or the bank rejects the foreign investment report due to a deficiency, file an amended report with a corrected investment schedule or valuation certificate. If the Foreign Investment Registration Certificate is delayed, obtain an interim receipt and present it to the bank with conditional undertakings, then complete the certificate within the statutory cure period.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register workplace and statutory social insurance accounts
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Integrated Social Insurance Information Portal and local offices of the Ministry of Employment and Labor, National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Workers' Compensation and Welfare Service.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Within fourteen days after the commencement of business, register the Company as an employer in the four major social insurance schemes. File the workplace establishment report with the local Employment and Labor Office, employment insurance registration, industrial accident compensation insurance registration, national pension registration, and national health insurance and long-term care insurance registration. Provide the Business Registration Certificate, court registration extract, payroll roster, and employment contracts. For the Company's Payroll SaaS operation, also complete the personal information protection filings required under the Personal Information Protection Act so that payroll data may be lawfully processed on behalf of client employers.
required_dossiers: Business Registration Certificate
Court registration extract or certified certificate of registered matters
Payroll and employment roster as of business commencement
Representative director identification and corporate seal certificate
Workplace establishment report forms for the four social insurances
Personal information processing and privacy impact assessment documentation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a social insurance filing is queried, submit wage ledgers, employment contracts, and the payroll automation schedule. If the filing deadline was missed, accept the applicable surcharge, file a late report, and pay the assessed penalty. If the privacy filing is incomplete, commission a privacy impact assessment and submit the correction to the Personal Information Protection Commission.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not Applicable - the Company will conduct only ISIC 6201 digital programming, software development, and cloud-based payroll SaaS services; no physical manufacturing, chemical, assembly, or warehousing activity is registered.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Not Applicable - no separate operating license is required for ISIC 6201 under the Korean positive licensing list; the Company must maintain its Business Registration Certificate and, if processing personal data, comply with Personal Information Protection Act registration and privacy impact assessment obligations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Environment, Republic of Korea - Not Applicable for this digital-only operation.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No EIA tier is applicable; environmental impact assessment is not required for computer programming or payroll SaaS services, and no construction, manufacturing, chemical, or warehousing facility will be established.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not Applicable currently; zero wastewater discharge, zero VOC emissions, and zero hazardous waste generation are associated with the registered digital business. If the Company later installs office backup generators or leases industrial storage, the thresholds of the Clean Air Conservation Act and the Water Quality Conservation Act would be assessed at that time.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not Applicable as a pre-formation operating license. For a pure digital office, the building owner must maintain a lawfully issued fire-fighting systems completion certificate and emergency evacuation plan, and the Company must comply with the Occupational Safety and Health Act for office employees; however, no Civil Defense fire permit or industrial safety clearance is triggered by ISIC 6201 software development.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) of the Republic of Korea; electronic portal: NTS HomeTax (www.hometax.go.kr)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For the declared Korean Chusik Hoesa, the entity will obtain its 10-digit Business Registration Number (BRN, which functions as the TIN and VAT registration ID) by filing the prescribed business registration application with the district tax office that has jurisdiction over the registered head office; filing is performed electronically on HomeTax after incorporation with the Commercial Act registry. For a foreign non-resident entity with a Korean establishment or a Korean-source activity, the procedure requires: (1) appointing a tax representative if no fixed place of business exists in Korea; (2) completing the HomeTax business registration application, including the foreign entity registration certificate, constitutional documents, proof of the Korean place of business, and the power of attorney for the tax representative; (3) submitting the application to the local district tax office; (4) receiving the BRN and VAT registration certificate. Registration is governed by Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act and the Framework Act on National Taxes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box or pass-through election is available because a Chusik Hoesa is mandatorily a resident corporation subject to entity-level taxation; qualifying Korean corporate groups may, however, elect joint consolidated group taxation under the Corporate Tax Act, and transfer pricing/foreign tax credit elections may be made through annual tax returns and advance pricing agreements with the NTS.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Value-Added Tax) under the Korean Value-Added Tax Act
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No monetary threshold applies; every person, including a foreign non-resident entity carrying on a business in Korea, is required to file for business/VAT registration under Article 8 of the Value-Added Tax Act within 20 days from the business commencement date regardless of turnover, with simplified taxpayer treatment available only to qualifying small service/retail businesses.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Korea operates a centralized real-time e-invoice regime: all VAT-registered taxpayers must issue an electronic tax invoice (digital tax invoice) for each taxable supply and transmit it to the NTS HomeTax e-invoice platform via the approved API/ERP integration on the date of supply or no later than the next business day, as prescribed by the Value-Added Tax Act. There is no advance transaction-level fiscal approval or physical digital stamp, but the NTS applies automated matching, e-invoice serial-number controls, and risk-based detection of paper-to-digital manipulation; late or failed transmission triggers per-invoice penalties.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A 0% VAT rate applies under Article 24 of the Value-Added Tax Act to exported goods and services supplied to overseas non-residents where the place of supply is outside Korea, including qualifying offshore SaaS, software, payroll platform, and digital-services subscriptions supplied from Korea to foreign business customers. To sustain the zero rate the supplier must create and retain written contracts, invoices, customs evidence, and bank payment records capable of demonstrating that title/control passed outside Korea, the beneficial user is a foreign business/government, payment is collected from abroad, and foreign currency is received in Korea through a Foreign Exchange Bank.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs export declaration acceptance/export declaration number issued by Korea Customs Service
Commercial invoice and underlying contract evidencing the supply to the overseas buyer
Ocean Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or other shipping/electronic-lading evidence of international movement
Foreign Exchange Bank inward payment certificate or foreign-currency repatriation evidence proving actual collection of export/SaaS consideration
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: If the NTS determines that the zero-rating is not substantiated by the required contemporaneous documentation or that the export proceeds are not repatriated to Korea by the 180th day, it may retroactively reclassify the supply as taxable at 10%, issue a revised assessment with late-payment interest, impose statutory penalties under the Value-Added Tax Act and Framework Act on National Taxes (including up to 40% of the unpaid tax for fraudulent under-declaration and 10-20% negligence penalties), and pursue criminal sanctions under the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act for willful evasion or false e-invoice issuance.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Korea, acting as the central bank and principal operator of the Foreign Exchange Information System FEPIS, together with the Ministry of Economy and Finance as the foreign exchange policy authority and licensed foreign exchange banks as delegated executing intermediaries
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: South Korea operates a liberalised but fully monitored foreign exchange environment under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act and the Enforcement Decree on Foreign Exchange Transactions. Current-account transactions, including payroll licensing, software subscription revenues, consulting fees and trade payments, are generally freely convertible in KRW, provided the underlying income is supported by commercial contracts, tax invoices and payment purpose declarations filed through the Foreign Exchange Information System FEPIS. Capital-account transactions are subject to pre-reporting or post-reporting requirements; foreign direct investment into a Chusik Hoesa is permissible but must be routed through a registered foreign exchange bank and registered with the Ministry of Economy and Finance. There is no general surrender requirement for export proceeds; Korean companies may maintain foreign-currency deposit accounts and retain export earnings in foreign currency. The main convertibility hurdles are documentary rather than exchange-control-imposed: inward remittances require the foreign investor to file a capital transaction report, and outward dividends, principal repayments or cross-border technology royalties require a validated foreign exchange rate, withholding tax verification from the National Tax Service and a filing with the Bank of Korea. In practice, a foreign-owned payroll automation company must maintain a robust transfer-pricing file, audited accounts, software licensing contracts and payroll service agreements to demonstrate commercial substance before profit repatriation or large cross-border disbursements are approved.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Foreign Exchange Transactions Regulations, export proceeds for goods must be received in the Republic of Korea within 18 months of the export customs declaration, unless a foreign exchange bank grants an extension, normally up to one additional year, for documented trade delays or settlement disputes. Services export proceeds, including software and payroll-processing revenues, must be reported to the foreign exchange bank in the applicable monthly foreign exchange information statement. There is currently no mandatory conversion ratio to KRW; Korean exporting entities may hold all export receipts in foreign currency deposit accounts, and the effective surrender ratio for proceeds is zero percent.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low viability as a primary treasury banker. South Korea does not grant full banking licences to offshore fintech EMI providers, and an overseas electronic money institution cannot lawfully hold a Chusik Hoesa local KRW settlement account or execute direct debit payroll rails. A fintech EMI may only transact through a Korean licensed bank sponsor, creating a nested account arrangement that Korean anti-money laundering compliance committees typically reject for a medium-risk SaaS treasury due to third-party counter-party risk. A fintech EMI may be acceptable only as a supplementary outbound cross-border beneficiary interface, never as the regulated domestic account structure.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Most tier-one Korean banks require at least one statutory director or a registered attorney-in-fact physically present at the branch for an in-person know-your-client interview when opening a Chusik Hoesa operating account, especially with non-resident shareholders. Remote consular proxy opening is permitted only on a case-by-case basis after notarised general power of attorney, apostille, source-of-funds documentation and affirmative approval by the bank compliance committee. Korean resident directors or compliance delegates are strongly preferred because the Real-Name Financial Transactions Act and actual transaction verification guidance impose personal accountability for the authorised signatory.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership chain involving intermediate foreign holding companies and nominee ownership risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified international corporate extract; full shareholder equity chain diagram; register of directors and shareholders for every intermediate holding entity; audited financial statements for the ultimate parent and immediate parent; sworn beneficial ownership declaration; certificate of good standing from each foreign jurisdiction; 24-month bank statements showing the original source of funds for capital injection.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payroll SaaS business with multi-country employee payments triggers suspicion of unlicensed money transmission or remittance aggregation
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Business constitution documents; enterprise customer contracts; software-as-a-service license agreements; payroll processing service descriptions; underlying employment or contractor agreements; screenshots of HR payroll automation workflows; anti-money laundering, counter-terrorist financing and sanctions policies; ISMS/PISMS or international information security certification; explanation of fee-based, non-custodial payroll model.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Exposure of cross-border technology transfers and personal payroll data to high-risk jurisdictions or sanctioned parties
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Data protection impact assessment under the Korean Personal Information Protection Act; client country matrix excluding comprehensively sanctioned jurisdictions; export control and encryption classification memo; OFAC/EU/UN sanctions screening results; PEP declarations for all shareholders and directors; adverse media and negative news analysis; representation letter from corporate counsel confirming no prohibited military or nuclear applications.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Thin substance mismatch between the Korean Chusik Hoesa and its declared software development, sales and payroll operation activity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified Korean business registration certificate; registered office lease agreement and utility bills; local employee payroll records and National Pension, National Health Insurance and Employment Insurance filings; board minutes authorising account opening; technology infrastructure agreements with cloud service providers; corporate income tax returns for the previous filing period; transfer-pricing contemporaneous documentation for intra-group service fees and software royalty structures.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The foreign investor must first obtain a Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, then open a restricted foreign-currency Capital Escrow Account at a tier-one licensed foreign exchange bank. The inbound capital injection must arrive by SWIFT MT103 wire with the purpose code for foreign direct investment and the beneficiary name matching the registered Chusik Hoesa. Upon controlled receipt, the bank executes the foreign exchange purchase declaration, submits the capital transaction report to the Bank of Korea through FEPIS, and releases funds to the KRW operating account only after the share issuance is verified. A certified public accountant must issue the final capital verification report based on the bank inward remittance certificate, the foreign investment certificate and the directors board resolution approving share subscription.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound payments should use SWIFT MT103 for international payroll vendors and suppliers, with the correct ISO 20022 purpose code and supporting commercial contracts. For large-scale equipment or licence procurement, commercial letters of credit and documentary collections are acceptable rail structures. Domestic Korean employee payroll disbursements use Direct Debit ACH with bank payroll files; cross-border payroll can be executed through the foreign exchange bank mass payment API, with each outgoing transfer accompanied by a payment purpose declaration, underlying agreement, tax invoice and FEPIS actual payment report submitted to the Bank of Korea.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore KRW/USD deliverable forward contracts backed by underlying trade or service receivables and payables, not exceeding real exposure
Cross-currency swaps and interest rate swaps associated with foreign-currency financing or capital transactions, subject to bank approval and Bank of Korea reporting
Covered currency options for hedging margin and gross revenue flows, provided the notional does not exceed documented foreign-currency exposure

Offshore KRW non-deliverable forward contracts permitted only where the transaction is booked through a licensed domestic bank to hedge valid exposure and is reported to the Bank of Korea under the foreign exchange information system, with speculative use prohibited

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual General Meeting (AGM) convened and financial statements/appropriation of income approved by shareholders
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Company board of directors and shareholders' meeting; minutes retained in the corporate registered office; where audited, the finalized financial statements must be delivered to shareholders and notice to FSS/KICPA is made under the External Audit Act as applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within three months after each fiscal year-end; for a December 31 fiscal year, no later than March 31; notice must be dispatched at least 21 days before the meeting
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: No direct filing fine, but directors who fail to call or approve within the statutory window may incur civil liability for shareholder losses and court-ordered convocation; companies subject to external audit that fail to present audited statements may be penalized by the Financial Supervisory Service and by the court on application of shareholders or creditors

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual corporate income tax return and self-assessment package under the Corporate Tax Act, including financial statement attachments and tax credits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) via the HomeTax electronic filing portal; local municipality receives the parallel local corporate income tax report where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By the last day of the third month after fiscal year-end; for December 31 year-end, due March 31; filing extension request by the deadline grants up to two additional months
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or underpaid corporate tax incurs additional tax equal to 20-40% of the underpaid amount depending on intentionality, plus monthly overdue interest calculated at the statutory NTS interest rate currently about 3.5% per annum; consistent non-filing can trigger collection seizure and criminal referral under the Tax Offense Punishment Act

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Monthly payroll tax and social contribution remittances plus annual labor-income withholding statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: National Tax Service (NTS) for income tax withholding; National Pension Service, National Health Insurance Service, and Korea Employment and Welfare Service for social premiums
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Monthly payroll tax and social premium payments due by the 10th of the following month; annual labor-income withholding report due by March 10 of the following calendar year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late withholding deposits attract NTS additional tax currently 3% per month up to 30% for delinquency plus fixed underreporting penalties; social insurance authorities impose daily or monthly delinquency surcharges and may execute collection procedures

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Independent statutory auditor engagement and audited financial statements submitted to the AGM when mandatory audit threshold is met
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Independent CPA or certified audit firm registered with the Korean Institute of Certified Public Accountants (KICPA); the auditor's report must be attached to the financial statements presented to shareholders and, if required, filed with the Financial Supervisory Service
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually before the ordinary AGM; for a December 31 fiscal year-end, audited financial statements and auditor's report must be available to shareholders ahead of the March 31 AGM; FSS filing, if triggered, is made promptly after approval or within the regulatory filing calendar prescribed under the External Audit Act
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A company exceeding the statutory audit threshold that fails to engage a registered external auditor is liable to administrative fines under the External Audit Act and the court registry may refuse to record director re-appointments; false or unreviewed statements can trigger criminal penalties and monetary sanctions on the representative director and the auditor

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Commercial register updates for changes to directors, representative director, shareholders' ledger movements, by-laws, or registered office, and maintenance of current registration particulars
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Commercial Registration Office of the District Court in the company's jurisdictional region under the Korean Supreme Court Registration Network
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the event for registered-change items such as director resignations or appointments, head-office relocation, or amendment of articles; shareholder transfers must be recorded in the shareholders' register without unreasonable delay and maintained current for each AGM
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing subjects the company to statutory administrative penalties; matters not registered cannot be asserted against bona fide third parties, and registration negligence may serve as a basis for director liability claims

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory external audit is triggered by the Act on External Audit of Stock Companies, etc. The principal test is the balance-sheet asset threshold: external audit is required where total assets exceed KRW 12 billion (approx. USD 9.2 million) as of the close of the immediately preceding fiscal year. There is no Korean legal headcount or turnover threshold that, by itself, imposes an audit on a private stock corporation; however, a company must also submit to an independent audit if it is a listed/KOSPI/KOSDAQ/KONEX issuer, is designated as a public-interest company under the Capital Markets Act, is in a regulated financial sector subject to sectoral audit rules, or is otherwise ordered by the Financial Supervisory Service on application of shareholders or creditors. Payroll/HR SaaS platforms are not licensed financial companies, so for a non-listed private Chusik Hoesa the asset test is the operative threshold.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Korea IFRS (K-IFRS) applies to listed and public-interest companies; non-listed private companies may apply K-IFRS or Korean GAAP (generally accepted accounting principles in the Republic of Korea); eligible small entities may apply simplified SME accounting standards if consistent with external audit requirements.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The Republic of Korea does not maintain a general-purpose annual UBO confirmation or public beneficial ownership register for private stock companies. The company must keep and update the register of shareholders; any transfer of shares must be reflected in the register without unreasonable delay, and there is no separate 30-day UBO reporting window for ordinary share transfers in a private SaaS company. Under the Act on Reporting and Use of Certain Financial Transaction Information, certain obligations apply to financial institutions rather than to non-financial private entities. When external audit is mandatory, the external auditor inspects the register of members and related books; the statutory secretarial maintenance procedure therefore is to maintain an accurate share ledger, confirm identity of shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners for each AGM, and ensure tax filings reflect any ownership changes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% statutory top marginal rate for taxable income exceeding KRW 300 billion; progressive CIT brackets of 10% up to KRW 200 million, 20% from KRW 200 million to KRW 20 billion, 22% from KRW 20 billion to KRW 300 billion, and 25% above KRW 300 billion; plus a 10% local corporate income surtax producing an aggregate top effective marginal rate of 27.5%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Under the Special Taxation Limitation Act and the Foreign Investment Promotion Act: R&D tax credits may reach 25% to 50% of qualifying payroll automation software R&D; technology transfer and software algorithmic IP income may qualify for 50% corporate tax income deduction; venture SMEs and new venture companies may obtain 50% reduction for the first three years; foreign-invested businesses in Free Economic Zones, Economic Promotion Zones and special S/W clusters may obtain 5-year 100% CIT exemption followed by a 2-year 50% reduction, subject to prior approval and headcount and location conditions.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Korean Corporate Income Tax Return, National Tax Service Form 41, submitted through the HomeTax electronic filing portal (hometax.go.kr), together with the International Transaction Report schedule (Form 88), financial statements, and supplementary transfer pricing documentation schedules.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the closing day of the accounting period under Article 60(1) of the Corporate Tax Act; a December 31 fiscal year-end is due by March 31 of the following year, and if the due date falls on a non-business day, the next business day. Partner-level advance corporate tax payments apply semiannually for entities having a twelve-month accounting period.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Corporate legal identity and filing window: Chusik Hoesa legal name, business registration number, head office address, representative director name and date of birth, Korean taxpayer identification number, fiscal year beginning and end, and business code corresponding to ISIC 6201 / NAICS 541214 for automated global payroll and staff compliance software.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Enter the Korean TIN and indicate whether any shareholder or director is a non-resident. For a 100% foreign-owned Chusik Hoesa, attach the foreign shareholder register; board meetings, minutes, and key payroll software development decisions must be substantiated in Korea so that central management and control is not re-characterized as a foreign tax residence or a diverted digital economy enterprise.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income statement reconciliation: total book revenue from payroll SaaS subscriptions, implementation fees, HR compliance updates, direct debit ACH/SWIFT processing fees, customization, and annual maintenance, reconciled to gross income and deductible expenses under Korean corporate accounting standards and the Corporate Tax Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Preserve customer contracts, server logs, automated payroll calculation records, and interface evidence demonstrating Korean-source provision of the SaaS platform. Do not offshore the revenue merely because payment rails use global clearances; the place of business activity and contract acceptance generally establishes Korean source income for this Korean-resident entity.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax adjustment schedule: add-backs for non-deductible expenses, entertainment expenses exceeding statutory threshold, amortization and depreciation adjustments, bad debt provisions, fines, penalties, political contributions not deductible, and excessive non-arm's length related-party charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Any royalty, license, SaaS platform fee, central service charge, or interest payment to a non-resident related party may be deducted only if the expense satisfies the ordinary-and-necessary standard, has an executed contract, is economically substantiated, and has been reported in the transfer pricing schedules; a missing tax invoice or missing withholding record invalidates deduction.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base computation after NOL carryforward, non-taxable income, exemptions, and income deductions: starting with adjusted total income, deduct unused net operating losses, tax-exempt distributions, and statutory deductions to arrive at the final corporate income tax base.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Utilize the 10-year statutory NOL carryforward for losses arising from fiscal years beginning on or after January 1, 2016; large corporations are limited to a 60% deductibility of current taxable income net of carried-forward losses. Losses generated by a shell entity or artificial intercompany structure will be denied through the substance-over-form doctrine, leaving the tax base understated to be penalized as fraudulent understatement.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax and credits computation: apply progressive CIT rates, compute the 10% local corporate income surtax on the payable corporate tax, and deduct foreign tax credits, R&D credits, employment creation tax credits, temporary investment tax credits, and any gross-up credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign tax credit is available for foreign branch income only if the foreign underlying tax was actually paid and the income is included in the Korean tax base. No credit is allowed against Korean CIT for withholding tax that the Chusik Hoesa should have withheld on dividends paid to a non-resident parent; dividend WHT is a separate obligation of the Korean withholding agent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Foreign-related party transaction report (Form 88): itemized disclosure of cross-border controlled transactions by type including sales of goods, intercompany services, intellectual property license fees, payroll software royalties, lease payments, interest, loans, management fees, and cost-sharing arrangements with foreign related parties.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Disclose all outbound payments to the non-resident parent, IP holding affiliates, or regional hubs. State the selected arm's length method, comparable data, and intercompany agreement. If the aggregated related party transaction amount exceeds the statutory Local File threshold of KRW 10 billion or Master File threshold of KRW 50 billion, attach the contemporaneous documentation; failure to attach or substantiate the schedule is a separate compliance violation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Non-resident withholding and tax treaty declaration: declaration of dividends, interest, royalty, and other investment income paid to non-resident shareholders or associated enterprises, and determination of withholding tax at statutory or treaty-reduced rates.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For every outbound dividend, record the shareholder country of residence, shareholding percentage, Tax Residency Certificate number, and beneficial ownership declaration. Statutory withholding is 22% aggregate on dividends, interest, and royalties; a treaty-reduced rate may be applied only if the non-resident beneficiary submits a valid TRC and proves beneficial ownership and absence of treaty shopping.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Supplementary and anti-avoidance schedules: controlled foreign company income, foreign permanent establishment attribution, exit tax adjustments, books and records declarations, and attached audited financial statements if required by the External Audit Act.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: If the Chusik Hoesa has foreign subsidiaries, a CFC schedule must be completed; the Korean entity must show that core income-generating activities, including payroll automation R&D, HR regulatory compliance, data hosting, and client service, are actually carried out in Korea and that no foreign branch has assumed the profit-bearing function in a way that deprives Korea of taxing rights.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without a justifiable cause triggers 20% of the unpaid tax as an additional penalty; underpayment by omission triggers 10%; fraudulent understatement or concealment triggers 40%; late payment adds 0.022% per day from the statutory due date. Failure to withhold non-resident tax triggers collection of the full unwithheld amount from the Korean payer plus 20% under-withholding penalty, and, if fraudulent, the criminal provisions of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act apply with imprisonment up to 7 years and fines up to twice the evaded tax; an aggregate tax delinquency may also support a Taiwanese-style departure blacklist? Actually in Korea the National Tax Service can request a travel block for unpaid delinquent tax over statutory thresholds, and directors may be barred from leaving Korea.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 22% aggregate statutory withholding on outbound dividends, composed of 20% national corporate income tax withheld at source and 2% local corporate income tax surtax; this is reduced only when a bilateral Korea tax treaty provides a lower rate to a beneficial owner meeting documentary and holding-period conditions.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To claim DTA relief, the non-resident shareholder must, before remittance or with the first dividend payment, file with the Korean withholding agent an application for tax-treaty withholding reduction using the National Tax Service's treaty relief process, attaching an original Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the residence country tax authority, a beneficial ownership certificate, evidence of shareholding percentage and minimum holding period required by the treaty, and documents proving the resident has economic substance and is not a conduit or back-to-back arrangement. The Korean payer must retain the approved documents in the withholding tax file and submit a withholding tax return to the NTS; if treaty relief was not obtained before remittance, the over-withheld tax may be reclaimed through a refund claim filed within three years under the Framework Act on National Taxes.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory withholding on interest and royalties is 22% aggregate (20% national plus 2% local surtax). Under an applicable DTA, interest is commonly reduced to 10% and royalties to 10% or 15%, with lower or zero rates possible if the recipient is the beneficial owner and no Korean permanent establishment exists. For payroll software SaaS, the distinction between a deductible license royalty for the software algorithms and a taxable technical service fee is critical: subscription fees that merely enable automated payroll processing without transfer of the right to exploit the payroll source code may be recharacterized by the NTS as taxable royalties or service income; the withholding agent must determine the character from the actual contract, not the label.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: A mandatory Local File must be prepared when cross-border related-party transaction amounts exceed KRW 10 billion in a fiscal year; a Master File is required when the multinational group's related-party transactions exceed KRW 50 billion or the group's consolidated annual revenue exceeds KRW 100 billion, and specific categories of services, intangibles, loans, and goods have separate lower reporting thresholds requiring an annual International Transaction Report where services or intangibles exceed KRW 50 million or goods exceed KRW 100 million.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Korea does not operate the Gulf Cooperation Council Economic Substance Regulations regime, but the substance-over-form principle in Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the Business Restructuring rules under the International Tax Adjustment Act, and the OECD principal purposes test require the Korean payroll SaaS entity to demonstrate Core Income-Generating Activities in Korea. The CIGA of payroll automation include proprietary payroll engine development, HR regulatory updates, salary calculation algorithms, data storage, employee compliance monitoring, and client management; an entity that merely executes contracts and invoices while the foreign affiliate performs all real functions and bears no substantive risk may be disregarded, its intercompany prices adjusted, and its treaty benefits denied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion Through Suppressed Payroll SaaS Revenue and Digital Payment Diversion
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Intentionally failing to recognize Korean subscription, customization, and direct-debit processing revenue by installing a zero-employee Hong Kong-based invoicing intermediary that receives SWIFT ACH wire traffic from Korean clients while the Chusik Hoesa's software servers, developers, payroll compliance team, and board decisions remain in Korea; issuing non-verified tax invoices or deliberately omitting revenue from Form 41.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act and Article 60 of the Corporate Tax Act; under Articles 47-2 and 47-4 of the Framework Act on National Taxes, the civil deficiency can be computed as 100% of the omitted corporate tax plus 40% understatement penalty for fraudulent act plus 0.022% daily late-payment interest. Criminal exposure is imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to twice the amount of tax evaded.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The National Tax Service may pierce the corporate veil under Supreme Court substance-over-form precedent and FANT Article 14 when the Chusik Hoesa is a shell used for tax evasion; the representative director and CFO who signed the false return or directed the hidden digital revenue are jointly and severally liable for unpaid corporate tax, interest, and penalties from personal assets, may face a departure ban or immigration blacklist for tax delinquency, and may be criminally imprisoned; under Commercial Act Article 401 the directors also owe civil damages to creditors for gross negligence in payroll SaaS revenue diversion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Wilful Non-Withholding on Outbound Dividends, Interest, and Royalties
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a foreign parent or paying software royalties and intercompany loan interest to a non-resident affiliate without withholding the statutory 22% aggregate tax, or applying a zero or reduced DTA rate using a sham Tax Residency Certificate, a back-to-back contract intended to divert income through a third treaty country, or without evidence of beneficial ownership and economic substance in the treaty jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 98, 98-5 and 98-6 of the Corporate Tax Act and Articles 47-4 and 47-5 of the Framework Act on National Taxes: the Korean payer is liable to collect and remit the full 22% withholding tax, is denied any deduction for the gross-up absent withholding, and is subject to a 20% under-withholding penalty and 0.022% daily late-payment surcharge. If the non-withholding was fraudulent, the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act applies with imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine up to twice the unwithheld tax.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The director or finance officer who deliberately failed to withhold may be personally liable for the unwithheld amount under FANT Article 12, since the company is merely a fiduciary withholding agent; the NTS may collect the unwithheld amount from the director's personal bank accounts and request a prohibition on departure from Korea until the under-withheld tax is settled. Criminal conviction also triggers disqualification of the representative director and civil restitution claims by the Korean treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham Shell IP Holding and Transfer Pricing Documentation Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a foreign affiliate as nominal owner of the payroll SaaS intellectual property source code, algorithms, and trademarks, having the Korean operating Chusik Hoesa pay excessive royalties to that affiliate without any technical staff, board function, or risk-taking by the foreign IP holder, and completely omitting the mandatory Local File, Master File, and Form 88 international transaction report when cross-border related-party transactions exceed KRW thresholds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Articles 4, 4-2 and 5 of the International Tax Adjustment Act permit the NTS to re-determine the arm's length royalty and constructive dividend, to deny the related-party royalty deduction, and to impose additional tax under Article 19 of that Act; unreported or understated international transactions may incur 10% to 30% penalties and the 40% fraud penalty under FANT Article 47-4; the statute of limitations for assessment is extended for fraudulent omission. The arrangement may be recharacterized as an abusive tax avoidance scheme under Article 14 of the Framework Act on National Taxes.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The NTS will disregard the foreign subsidiary and attribute its CIGA and income to the Korean entity, and if the director causes the limited company to be used for a sham IP tax shelter, the corporate veil may be pierced; the director is jointly and severally liable for the unpaid tax, can be blacklisted from international travel, and under Article 9 of the Punishment of Tax Evaders Act can face imprisonment up to 7 years and a fine equal to twice the understated corporate tax deficiency, while Commercial Act Article 401 exposes the director to shareholder and creditor damage claims for the sham structure.
